chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nuḍr ibn Suwayd from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: When a man has two sisters who are enslaved, and he marries one of them, then decides to marry the second, he should not marry the other until the first leaves his ownership, whether by him gifting her or selling her. And if he gifts her to his son, it suffices him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for marrying two enslaved sisters?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the Shia juristic view on 'Jam' al-Akhtayn' (simultaneous possession of two sisters) in slavery, requiring the removal of the first sister from ownership—via sale or gift—to permit marriage to the second. Notably, it specifies that gifting the sister to one's own son is a valid method of severing the ownership link, a nuance that distinguishes it from some Sunni interpretations which may require the gift to be to a non-heir or involve actual transfer of possession. This ruling underscores the principle that the impediment is based on concurrent ownership rather than the marital bond itself.
